newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian government refuses to delay election.
newsitem.headline: Croatian government refuses to delay election.

text.p: The Croatian goverment on Tuesday rejected the opposition Social Liberal party's demand for a postponement of Sunday's presidential election after its candidate Vlado Gotovac was attacked at a campaign rally.

"The government could not accept Mr Gotovac's demand because there are no constitutional or legal grounds for it. The law on presidential elections does not foresee the possibility of setting new dates for electoral activities," said a brief government statement carried by state radio.

Gotovac's Social Liberal party (HSLS) called for a two-week delay after a Croatian army officer struck him on the head with a belt buckle at a rally last week. It also complained the authorities had not done enough to protect the candidates.

"The reason for this is the attempt on the life of Vlado Gotovac in Pula...when he sustained such injuries that he was thrown out of the presidential race," party secretary Karl Gorinsek told a news conference.
The 66-year old Gotovac, who suffered concussion and neck injuries, was released from hospital on Sunday but doctors said on Monday he had to refrain from any activity and stay in bed.
The HSLS asked for both other candidates, President Franjo Tudjman and Zdravko Tomac of the Social Democrats, to stop campaigning until Gotovac was better.
Gorinsek said the party would reconsider whether Gotovac would run in Sunday's polls after the goverment replied to their demand.

The party released the findings of a doctor's examination which found that Gotovac was suffering from a recurrence of neck injuries which he sustained during his time in prison after he was jailed for supporting Croatia's pro-independence movement in the 1970s.

The man who attacked Gotovac was a captain in the Croatian army and was in uniform at the time. The ministry of defence named him as Tomislav Brzovic, said he was drunk at the time of the attack and immediately suspended him from duty and detained him.

The Liberal party and independent weekly news magazine Feral Tribune both alleged Brzovic was a member of Tudjman's elite security guard, though this has not been confirmed by the ministry of defence.

State news agency HINA reported on Tuesday the public prosecutor in Pula requested that Brzovic be kept in custody for one month and investigation against him started, based on suspicions that he committed an act of violent behaviour.
Both opposition candidates are fighting a losing battle to try and oust Tudjman, who is widely expected to win the election in the first round with 60-70 percent of votes.
They face fawning state-run media which run at length many of the president's official engagements, ensuring he benefits from more coverage than his opponents do.
